Psychometric score measuring how well the question separates strong from weak students.

This measures how well a question separates your strong students from your weak ones. A good question should be answered correctly by strong students and incorrectly by weak ones.
Classic Formula (Upper/Lower 27% method — used in NAPLAN & psychometrics)
D=Cupper−ClowernD = \frac{C_{upper} - C_{lower}}{n}D=nCupper​−Clower​​
Where:

C_upper = number of correct answers from the top 27% of students (ranked by total exam score)
C_lower = number of correct answers from the bottom 27% of students
n = total number of students in each group (i.e. 27% of total cohort)

Step-by-step example
Say you have 100 students who sat the exam:

Rank all 100 students by their total exam score
Take the top 27 (upper group) and bottom 27 (lower group)
For a specific question, count how many in each group got it right:

Upper group: 22 correct → C_upper = 22
Lower group: 8 correct → C_lower = 8
n = 27

Then D = (22-8)/27 = 0.52
